title: Privacy Policy
intro: Bannergress is a community project for discovering and sharing Ingress mission banners. This policy explains how the Bannergress team handles personal data when you use bannergress.com, its API, and its sign-in service.

account.title: Sign-in and account data
account.body:
You can browse public banners without signing in. If you choose Google sign-in, our authentication service, Keycloak, receives the provider's account identifier and the basic profile information supplied for sign-in, such as your email address, name, and profile picture. We do not receive your Google password.

Keycloak stores your Bannergress account, its link to the sign-in provider, and profile information. For Google sign-in, this includes your Google account identifier and profile picture URL. Bannergress uses its own user UUID to associate your account with your saved data. The website displays your username and profile picture to you when you are signed in.

Google access is used for sign-in and basic profile information. We do not request access to Gmail, Google Drive, Google Contacts, or Google Calendar. Google access tokens are used during authentication and are not stored in your Bannergress account; Bannergress issues its own session tokens.

use.title: How and why we use data
use.body:
We use account data to sign you in, maintain your session, save your banner lists, verify an Ingress account link you request, and check permissions for contributions and edits. We also process information needed to answer support requests, operate the service, and investigate errors or abuse.

Our servers receive connection information such as your IP address, request time, requested URL, and browser information. Operational and security logs may contain this information. We do not sell personal data or use Google account data for advertising. The website does not use advertising cookies or third-party analytics trackers.

Where applicable data protection law requires a legal basis, we process data as necessary to provide the service you request, for our legitimate interests in operating and protecting it, or to comply with legal obligations. Optional device location and third-party account access depend on your permission or consent.

contributions.title: Banner lists, Ingress links, and contributions
contributions.body:
We store your todo, done, and hidden (blacklist) banner selections, the time a banner was added to a list, and your Bannergress user UUID. These personal lists are associated with your account and are not published as public lists.

If you link an Ingress account, we store the agent name and verification information and associate the verified agent with your Bannergress account. You can unlink it on the account page.

Banners and mission information you submit, including titles, descriptions, images, routes, and agent names, are intended to be shared with other users. We keep a change history for contributions that can include the editing user's identifier and the time of the change. Do not include private information in public contributions.

location.title: Location, maps, and external content
location.body:
If you use a locate or proximity feature and allow browser location access, the website uses your coordinates to show your position or find nearby banners. For proximity searches, coordinates are sent to the Bannergress API. Map searches also send the visible map bounds. You can refuse or withdraw location permission in your browser settings.

Maps load tiles directly from OpenStreetMap servers. Tile requests reveal your IP address, browser information, and the map area requested to that provider. See the OpenStreetMap Foundation Privacy Policy. Profile pictures and mission images may also load from Google, which receives the connection information needed to deliver them.

Following external links, such as Google Maps directions, Ingress, or Telegram support, connects you to those services. Their own privacy policies apply; a directions link includes the selected destination coordinates.

storage.title: Cookies, browser storage, and security
storage.body:
Our sign-in service uses cookies to manage authentication and remember your session, including when you choose to stay signed in. The website uses session storage for preferences, searches, map position, and scroll position; proximity preferences can include coordinates. You can clear this data in your browser. Clearing cookies may sign you out.

Connections to the production website, API, and sign-in service use HTTPS. Bannergress session tokens authorize API requests. Account and list data are stored in the authentication and backend databases, with access controlled by authentication and permissions. Authorized maintainers may access data as needed for support, maintenance, security, or legal obligations.

sharing.title: Third-party access with your consent
sharing.body:
You can explicitly authorize a third-party application to access your Bannergress account. Access is granted only after you approve the consent screen.

This integration identifies you by your Bannergress user UUID and does not forward your Google profile name, email address, or profile picture to the authorized application. The authorization token also contains technical information needed for authentication. Your UUID is a pseudonymous account identifier, not anonymous data.

An authorized application can use its token to access Bannergress account data through the API, including your todo, done, and hidden lists and Ingress linking information. The API also allows authenticated applications to update banner-list selections. Consent therefore permits access to personal account data even though sign-in provider profile details are not forwarded.

You can withdraw an application's authorization in the sign-in service's account settings or contact Bannergress support for help. Already issued access tokens can remain valid until they expire, and withdrawing authorization does not delete copies previously obtained by the third party. Consult that application's privacy policy and contact it about those copies.

Infrastructure providers process information needed to host and deliver the service. We may also disclose information when required by law or necessary to protect the service against abuse. Our use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adhere to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including its Limited Use requirements.

retention.title: Retention and deletion
retention.body:
Account information and saved lists are kept to provide your account and its features. You can change or remove list selections and unlink your Ingress account yourself. To request deletion of your Bannergress account and associated personal data, contact Bannergress support. We may need to verify that the account belongs to you.

Signing out, unlinking Ingress, or removing Google access does not by itself delete your Bannergress account or lists. Public contributions and change histories are separate from your private account data; when requesting deletion, you can also ask about personal information in those records. Some records may need to be retained to meet legal obligations or investigate abuse.

rights.title: Your choices and privacy contact
rights.body:
Contact the Bannergress team through Telegram Support for privacy questions or requests to access, correct, export, or delete your personal data. Please ask for a private conversation before sharing account details in a support chat.

You can remove Bannergress's Google authorization through your Google Account connections. This is separate from withdrawing a third-party application's access to Bannergress. You can also control cookies, browser storage, and location permissions in your browser.

Depending on the law that applies to you, you may have rights to restrict or object to processing, receive a portable copy of your data, withdraw consent, and complain to a data protection authority. Withdrawing consent does not affect processing already carried out lawfully.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: We will update this page and its revision date when our privacy practices change. If we introduce a new use of Google account data or new third-party access that requires consent, we will explain it and request that consent before the new use begins.
